claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I was wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 16, I need to ask some questions to determine your eligibility, as the rules change when a child reaches that age.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he studying at school, college, or doing an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is an important detail for Alex's eligibility.

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he has, you may still be able to get Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after leaving education or training.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that yet. He's just been at home since leaving school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Has Alex started any paid work? If so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question to complete my assessment:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not claiming any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me carefully assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on the rules.

According to the UK Child Benefit rules:

- You normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child under 16
- For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if they are under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training
- You can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education or training

In Alex's situation:
- He is 16 years old
- He is not in approved education or training
- He has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services
- He is not working

Since Alex is 16, not in approved education or training, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Once a child reaches 16, Child Benefit can only continue if they remain in approved education or training (up to age 20). Since Alex has left school and is not in any approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.

However, there may be an option available: If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you could potentially claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education. This might give you some support while he decides on his next steps.

I hope this information is helpful, even though it's not the answer you were hoping for. If Alex does enter education, training, or registers with a careers service, your situation would change and you should contact HMRC to update them.
